name: patchwork-vscode
description: Review code from your phone using local LAN or an HTTPS tunnel.

patchwork.autoStart.description: Start the read-only companion when VS Code finishes starting with a workspace open.

patchwork.port.description: LAN port used by the Patchwork companion. Use 0 to choose an available port automatically.

enumDescriptions: Try verified Codex then Claude Code subscription logins. Never automatically use API billing.
Use the locally authenticated Codex CLI subscription.
Use the locally authenticated Claude Code subscription.
Use the OpenAI Responses API configured in the companion environment.
Disable AI and keep the review interface available.
patchwork.aiProvider.description: AI provider used by the laptop companion. Local CLI providers reuse their existing laptop login.

patchwork.devAiLog.description: Development: record each AI request (prompt, repository tool calls, provider turns and answer) as private JSONL files in ~/.patchwork/ai-logs. Logs contain captured code and your questions. Restart the companion after changing this.

patchwork.companionPath.description: Optional absolute path to companion.mjs. Leave empty when developing from the Patchwork repository.

patchwork.cloudflaredPath.description: Path to the cloudflared executable used to create a temporary Cloudflare Quick Tunnel.

patchwork.tunnelName.description: Optional existing Cloudflare named tunnel to run. Patchwork does not create or configure this tunnel. Set patchwork.publicUrl and a fixed patchwork.port too.

patchwork.publicUrl.description: HTTPS public URL already routed by patchwork.tunnelName. It is used for phone pairing and preserves the same phone storage origin.

patchwork.startupTimeoutSeconds.description: Seconds to wait for the companion and tunnel to become ready before showing diagnostics.

patchwork.transport.description: Default connection: instant local LAN over HTTP, or an HTTPS tunnel. The pairing sidebar can switch between them.
